T-007's new AC-059 Done-When bullet (tasks.md:1910-1920) requires the grep self-check to scan `plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/validate-resolver-evidence.*`, but those files are authored by T-008, whose own Blockers field is 'T-001, T-006, T-007' (tasks.md:2182) -- i.e., T-008 is sequenced strictly AFTER T-007 and does not exist at T-007's own quality-gate/Done-When verification time. Unlike its stated model AC-025 (owned by T-009, whose own Blockers list 'T-002, T-003, T-004, T-005, T-006, T-007, T-008' (tasks.md region 2185-2340) place it downstream of every scanned script), AC-059's owner T-007 is not downstream of one of its own two named target globs. I confirmed by full read that T-008's own Requirements/Must Read/Done When (tasks.md:1986-2183) make zero mention of AC-059/TEST-059, so no task-level checkpoint anywhere in the package re-verifies the approval-surface write-scope lock against `validate-resolver-evidence.*` after those files actually exist. The package's own text ('registration-time and CI-gated,' tasks.md:1910-1912; acceptance-tests.md:120) does not establish that this is a perpetual, glob-based CI gate that automatically re-scans files added by later tasks, as opposed to a point-in-time verification at the owning task's own Done-When gate (the pattern every per-task 'Governance' bullet in this package uses instead, e.g., AC-032/AC-034, which ARE explicitly restated in every task including T-008's own). This ambiguity, combined with the complete absence of any AC-059 anchor in T-008, is a concrete integration-verification gap: a `validate-resolver-evidence.*` write violating the approval-surface boundary could land via T-008 with no Done-When item in the package ever catching it. This finding concerns only the AC-059 addition, reviewed on its own merits per the invocation's explicit carve-out from the TYPE-H convergence rule.
